DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Heart Disease (likely Large Left-to-Right Shunt) leading to High Output Failure and Anemia.

The combination of prematurity, placental insufficiency, a father with heart disease, and now documented apnea with signs of anemia strongly suggests a significant cardiac defect causing blood to shunt from the left side to the right side of the heart. This shunting causes pulmonary over-circulation (leading to apnea and respiratory distress) and dilutes red blood cells (causing anemia), while the heart works harder than it can manage, leading to fatigue and poor feeding. The history of placental insufficiency may have also contributed to the anemia through fetal-maternal hemorrhage. Immediate echocardiographic confirmation is required to determine the specific type of defect, such as a Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD) or Atrial Septal Defect (ASD), and to guide surgical intervention.
